rows.question: i have [[Hardened Scales]] and [[Doubling Season]] and cast ballista for X=2. how many counters does it come in with? do i get to pick the order or is it timestamps

Walking Ballista's 'enters with X +1/+1 counters' is a replacement effect (614.1c, 614.12), and Hardened Scales and Doubling Season are further replacement effects modifying the same event. When multiple replacement effects apply to the same event, the affected permanent's controller picks which applies first (616.1), and since none of the special priorities in 616.1a-d apply, any may be chosen (616.1e). Each effect applies only once to the event (614.5). Apply Scales first (2 -> 3), then Season doubles (3 -> 6). When two or more replacement effects try to modify the same event, the affected object's controller picks one to apply, then repeats the process with whatever still applies (616.1, 616.1f). Neither of these is a self-replacement, control-changing, copy or back-face effect, so you can choose either one first (616.1e). Each effect applies only once (614.5).

The Hardened Scales ruling says it directly: "you choose the order to apply those effects, no matter who controls the sources of those effects." Doubling Season's ruling also confirms it "affects permanents that enter with counters."

Urborg's effect depends on Blood Moon's (613.8a): applying Blood Moon makes Urborg a Mountain and strips its rules-text ability (305.7), which removes the existence of Urborg's effect. When a dependency exists it overrides timestamps (613.8), so Blood Moon applies first no matter which entered later (613.8b). outcome.answer:
Your friend is right. With **Blood Moon** out, **Urborg, Tomb of Yawgmoth** makes nothing a Swamp, and it doesn't matter which one came down first.

Both effects are type-changing effects, so both apply in layer 4. Normally timestamps would decide the order, but dependency comes first. rows.question: my goyf has two +1/+1 counters on it and I just giant growthed it. opponent [[Clone]]s it. is their clone a huge goyf too or just a regular one? and does the clone even know how big a goyf should be since the p/t is */*+1
rows.expected_answer: Just a regular Tarmogoyf. A copy acquires only the copiable values of the original (707.2): name, mana cost, types, rules text, printed P/T, etc. Counters, Giant Growth's +3/+3, and other non-copy effects are not copiable values, so the Clone gets none of them. The Clone does copy Tarmogoyf's rules text, and therefore its characteristic-defining ability (707.2a), so the Clone's own P/T is */*+1 computed from card types in graveyards (applied in layer 7a, 613.4a). The copy effect itself is applied in layer 1a (613.2a); your goyf's counters and pump are layer 7c (613.4c) and stay on your goyf only.

outcome.answer:
Their **Clone** is a regular **Tarmogoyf**. It doesn't get your two +1/+1 counters or the +3/+3 from **Giant Growth**, but it does copy the P/T-defining ability, so it is always exactly as big as a fresh Goyf.

Why: per `707.2`, a copy takes only the copiable values, which come from the printed text (name, types, rules text, power, toughness and so on). "Other effects (including type-changing and text-changing effects), status, counters, and stickers are not copied." Giant Growth's "Target creature gets +3/+3 until end of turn" is a non-copy effect, and the counters are counters, so neither carries over. The Clone ruling says the same thing: it doesn't copy counters "or any non-copy effects that have changed its power, toughness".

As for the */*+1, that P/T comes from rules text: "Tarmogoyf's power is equal to the number of card types among cards in all graveyards and its toughness is equal to that number plus 1." Per `707.2a`, a copy gets the abilities of what it copies, so the Clone has this ability too. It counts card types in all graveyards continuously, just like your Goyf. Example: if the graveyards hold creature, instant and land cards, the Clone is 3/4 and your Goyf is 3/4 + 2 counters + 3 = 8/9 until end of turn. Once Giant Growth resolves, the instant is in a graveyard and counts for both Goyfs.

rows.question: ok classic one. I have [[Humility]] out and my opponent drops [[Opalescence]]. what are Humility and Opalescence now?? are all my creatures still 1/1? does the answer change if Opalescence was out first?
rows.expected_answer: Walk the layers. Opalescence reads 'each OTHER non-Aura enchantment', so it never affects itself: Opalescence stays a noncreature enchantment and keeps its ability in every scenario. Layer 4 (613.1d): Opalescence makes Humility a 'creature' enchantment. Layer 6 (613.1f): Humility removes all abilities from every creature, including itself; per 613.6 an effect that has started applying keeps applying in later layers even though its source ability is gone. Layer 7b (613.4b): Humility's 'base P/T 1/1' and Opalescence's 'base P/T equal to mana value' both set Humility's P/T. Neither depends on the other under 613.8a (applying one doesn't change the text, existence, or targets of the other), so timestamp order decides (613.7). If Opalescence has the later timestamp: Humility is a 4/4 creature with no abilities. If Humility has the later timestamp: Humility is a 1/1 creature with no abilities. Either way every ordinary creature is a 1/1 with no abilities, and Opalescence is an unaffected noncreature enchantment. Any other non-Aura enchantment Opalescence animates follows Humility itself: its base power and toughness are its mana value when Opalescence is later, and 1/1 when Humility is.

outcome.answer:
Your regular creatures stay 1/1 with no abilities either way. **Opalescence** is never a creature, because it says "Each *other* non-Aura enchantment", so it keeps its ability. Only **Humility**'s own size depends on the order they arrived in.

**Humility out first (your case):** In layer 4, Opalescence turns Humility into an enchantment creature. In layer 6, Humility's effect removes all creature abilities, including Humility's own. Its effect still finishes applying anyway, per `613.6`: once an effect starts to apply, it keeps applying "even if the ability generating the effect is removed during this process." Both cards set power and toughness in layer 7b (`613.4b`). That sublayer goes in timestamp order (`613.7`), and neither effect depends on the other there. Humility's earlier effect makes every creature 1/1, then Opalescence's later effect makes Humility 4/4. Result: Humility is a 4/4 with no abilities, and your other creatures are 1/1 with no abilities.

**Opalescence out first:** Layers 4 and 6 work the same way. In 7b, Opalescence makes Humility 4/4 first, then Humility's later effect makes every creature 1/1, so Humility ends up 1/1 too. The Scryfall ruling on these two cards walks through exactly these two cases.

Other non-Aura enchantments work like Humility: they get their mana value if Humility came first, or 1/1 if Opalescence came first. Either way they lose their abilities.

rows.question: quick one: if I have [[Valki, God of Lies]] in hand can I just cast the Tibalt side for 7? and while it's in my library/graveyard does it count as a planeswalker card for stuff like Vraska's Contempt / Kaya's Ghostform?
rows.expected_answer: Yes. Valki // Tibalt is a modal double-faced card: when you cast it you choose which face you're casting before it goes on the stack, and only that face is evaluated (712.11b, 712.11c), so you can cast Tibalt, Cosmic Impostor for {5}{B}{R} straight from your hand. Once chosen, the spell/permanent has only that face's characteristics (712.8f). But anywhere other than the stack or battlefield (hand, library, graveyard, exile) an MDFC has only its front face's characteristics (712.8a), so it is a legendary creature card named Valki, God of Lies there — never a planeswalker card.

outcome.answer:
Yes, you can cast **Valki, God of Lies** as **Tibalt, Cosmic Impostor** for {5}{B}{R}. In your library or graveyard, though, it is only a Valki creature card with mana value 2. It is never a planeswalker card there.

Casting: when you cast a modal double-faced card, you choose which face you're casting before it goes on the stack (712.11b). Once Tibalt resolves, it's a planeswalker on the battlefield with only Tibalt's characteristics (712.8f).

Other zones: outside the battlefield and the stack, a double-faced card "has only the characteristics of its front face" (712.8a). The rulings say the same thing about mana value.

Your two examples only care about permanents, so this matters less than you might think:
- **Vraska's Contempt** can target Tibalt on the battlefield, because it's a planeswalker there.
- **Kaya's Ghostform** ("Enchant creature or planeswalker you control") can go on Tibalt. If Tibalt dies or is exiled, the Ghostform returns "that card" to the battlefield. A double-faced card put onto the battlefield from anywhere other than the stack enters front face up (712.14). So you get **Valki** back, not Tibalt. Valki's enter trigger will make each opponent reveal their hand again.

rows.question: I control a 2/2 with a Giant Growth resolving on it, and mid-resolution of a different spell it's technically at 0 toughness for a second (Maro-style hand-size thing). Does it die? And separately, if I have two Ragavan on the battlefield somehow, when exactly does the legend rule kick in - can I respond in between?
rows.expected_answer: 1) It doesn't die. State-based actions are only checked when a player would receive priority, not in the middle of a spell resolving (704.3, 704.4 - the CR's own Maro example). The creature only dies if it still has toughness 0 or less when SBAs are next checked (704.5f). 2) The legend rule (704.5j) is also a state-based action: the moment a player would get priority with two Ragavans you control, you choose one and the other goes to the graveyard. It doesn't use the stack and there is no window to respond between the second Ragavan entering and the legend rule applying; you can only respond before the second one enters/resolves.

outcome.answer:
No, it doesn't die, as long as its toughness is back above 0 when the spell finishes resolving. The legend rule kicks in the moment anyone would next get priority, so you can't respond with both **Ragavan**s on the battlefield.

**Zero toughness mid-resolution:** A creature only goes to the graveyard for 0 toughness when state-based actions are checked (704.5f). The game doesn't check them while a spell is resolving. Per 704.4, "state-based actions pay no attention to what happens during the resolution of a spell or ability." The CR's own example has **Maro** at toughness 0 partway through a resolution, back to 7 at the end, and it survives. The **Maro** ruling says the same: if its toughness hits 0 "and then goes back up above 0 before the end of that announcement or resolution, it won't be put into your graveyard." Only the toughness after the spell finishes resolving counts. If it's still 0 or less then, it dies.

**Two Ragavans:** The legend rule is a state-based action (704.5j). State-based actions happen automatically and don't use the stack (704.1). The game checks them "whenever a player would get priority" (704.3), before anyone actually gets priority (117.2d). So the moment both are on the battlefield, the next check makes you choose one, and the other goes to the graveyard before anyone gets priority. You can't cast spells or activate abilities in between, because nobody has priority during that window. Anything you want to do with the second Ragavan has to happen before the duplicate lands. Abilities that trigger on it going to the graveyard still trigger, and go on the stack afterward.

rows.question: commander q: my commander is [[Kenrith, the Returned King]]. two things: 1) can I run Nicol Bolas, the Ravager since Kenrith's text mentions all 5 colors? and 2) someone bounced Kenrith to my hand with Unsummon - does he go to the command zone or is that only for graveyard/exile?

outcome.answer:

A card can go in the deck if "every color in its color identity is also found in the color identity of the deck’s commander" (903.5c). Bolas is blue, black and red. rows.question: commander damage question. I've been hit for 15 by my opponent's Rafiq. she then copies it with a Clone and hits me for 6 more with the clone. do I lose? also does the 21 count noncombat damage like from Fling?
rows.expected_answer: No to both. A player loses when they've been dealt 21 or more COMBAT damage by the SAME commander over the course of the game (903.10a; checked as a state-based action, 704.6c). The Clone copying Rafiq is not a commander, so its 6 damage isn't commander damage - you're still at 15 from the real Rafiq. Fling damage is noncombat, so it never counts toward the 21 either; it just reduces your life total normally.

outcome.answer:
No, you don't lose. The **Clone** copying **Rafiq of the Many** is not a commander. Its 6 damage doesn't count toward Rafiq's total, so Rafiq's tally stays at 15. Damage from **Fling** never counts toward the 21 either, because it isn't combat damage.

Being a commander is a property of the card itself, not one of its characteristics (903.3). The rule says directly that "A permanent that’s copying a commander ... is not a commander." The Clone copies Rafiq's name, abilities and power, but not its commander status.

The loss condition in 903.10a has two requirements. The damage has to be combat damage, and it all has to come from the same commander. Fling deals noncombat damage: "Fling deals damage equal to the sacrificed creature's power to any target." So even if your opponent sacrifices the real Rafiq to Fling, that damage won't move you toward 21.

All of this damage still makes you lose life as normal (119.2). The Clone's hits and any Fling damage can still finish you off by bringing your life total to 0 (119.6). They just don't add to the 21-damage commander count.

rows.question: two quick ones. 1) if I tap all my lands during my upkeep does that mana stick around so I can cast the mind sculptor in my main phase? 2) when I'm casting snappy can I tap lands in the middle of casting it or do I have to float the mana first?
